stdio owner.instructions: This brain carries Recall: owner-authored memory maps and prompts for agents. Before starting a distinct task, call recall_match with one line describing it and apply a strong match. When working in a domain the owner has mapped, recall_index lists the maps — recall_open the relevant one and follow its options instead of searching blind. Pass intent= on recall_* calls (one line on why you came) so the owner's recall log can show it. Before building a mini app with the app_* tools, read app_authoring_guide: it covers host.me() (who runs the app), host.db, host.tools.call and the team and client level rules. A circuit drawn from the uploaded P&IDs is made the same way by every author, an agent here or a client over MCP: 1. `circuit_trace` with the circuit's name; 2. `circuit_verify` on the same circuit: each guess the trace made is asked about on a close-up crop of the drawing by the default vision model, which spends the owner's vision key (a few cents a circuit; dry_run lists the questions for free; it never runs on its own); 3. `circuit_trace` again, so the drawing carries the answers (CHECKED BY IMAGE, or FROM IMAGE where the image named what a guess really is); 4. save that `pid` object, unchanged, with `present_create` (or `present_update` for a saved drawing), once its pid_check is ok. `circuit_trace`, `present_create` and `present_update` report image_check: how many guesses on the drawing no image has checked, and the drawing shows that count until they are. Never drop or relabel a GUESS, CHECKED BY IMAGE or FROM IMAGE mark. Call `circuit_verify` at most once per trace in a turn, never again in the same turn for guesses it left out (not_asked, a cap, a time limit); save the drawing and report how many are unchecked. A second call within 10 minutes is refused unless `recheck`.
